Please review the following manuscript. I've poured days of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-dnu70ycx/call-060188b08f8c4870b7fcf6babc48fae1/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdfinfo; command -v pdftoppm; command -v python3; ls /fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/runtime/pdf'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, os
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
print('pdf_bytes', os.path.getsize('manuscript.pdf'))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages',len(r.pages))
print('metadata',r.metadata)
pages=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 pages.append(f'\\n--- PAGE {i} ---\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(pages))
print('\\n'.join(pages[:3]))
PY"

strengths: The paper connects interventionist explanations with causal discovery in a way that should interest researchers in model auditing and causal interpretability. This contribution does not depend on introducing a new algorithm or achieving state-of-the-art prediction accuracy.
Using partial ancestral graphs makes hidden confounding and orientation ambiguity explicit. Treating predictions as non-ancestors of image attributes provides sensible background knowledge.

The omitted-circle simulation makes the motivation concrete, while the bird and X-ray applications illustrate a practical workflow using existing annotations. The discussion usefully acknowledges limitations involving feature selection and background assumptions.
weaknesses: Necessary: Clarify the causal interpretation of macro-features. FCI's guarantees require an appropriate causal model of the observed variables; describing the annotation-level graph as a crude approximation does not establish this requirement. Changing an annotation, intervening on an underlying physical attribute, and editing pixels are different operations. Specify the assumed relationship among attributes, image generation, and predictions, and qualify the guarantees accordingly.

Necessary: Address selection bias in the X-ray experiment. Selecting pneumonia cases and controls with 'no findings' makes inclusion depend on diagnosis and the candidate findings. Conditioning on this selection can induce dependencies and invalidate the interpretation that Section II-B explicitly derives without selection bias. Model or otherwise justify the sampling mechanism, change the analysis population, or narrow the corresponding causal conclusions.

Necessary: Strengthen or narrow the simulation's conclusions. The known generating graph concerns Y, whereas the explanation targets the learned predictor Y-hat; 81% accuracy does not establish identical causal behavior. Controlled shape interventions on the trained network would directly check the claimed exclusions. Moreover, Section IV incorrectly states that H is marginally independent of Y and that R is independent of Y given C: the paths H ← U1 → V → Y and R ← H ← U1 → V → Y remain open. Correct these statements and clarify the implemented generating process.

Necessary: Interpret PAG uncertainty consistently. Figure 4(b) contains the possibly directed path H o–o V o→ Y-hat, so that graph does not rule out H as an indirect cause. More generally, absence of an adjacent causal edge does not exclude causal ancestry. Figure 6 also describes partially directed edges as indicating 'likely causes,' although they permit purely confounded explanations. Report definite and possible causes separately; their pooled bootstrap frequency is not a probability of causation.

Necessary: Establish the reliability of the conditional-independence tests. The X-ray analysis has only 239 images and potentially rare findings, while the bird analysis conditions on combinations of categorical attributes. Report relevant contingency-table sparsity diagnostics and assess sensitivity to the significance thresholds and conditioning-set limit. Bootstrap repetition does not repair poorly calibrated chi-squared tests, and the four-variable conditioning cap requires qualification of the unrestricted FCI consistency claim.

Necessary: Resolve reporting inconsistencies and supply essential analysis details. The bird splits sum to 3,898, not the reported 3,538 images. A single accuracy of 74.55% is incompatible with an unweighted test set of 50 images unless an additional averaging procedure was used. Identify which predictions entered graph discovery, clarify patient-level sampling for X-rays, and provide the category and attribute mappings deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied manuscript.

Optional: An associational feature-ranking comparison would make clearer which conclusions causal discovery changes. Additional simulation repetitions and architectures would help characterize the workflow's scope.
